title: Who is St. Mark the Apostle?
text: St. Mark the Apostle brought the good news of Jesus to Egypt. He wrote the Gospel of Mark, and the Church teaches that he was the first Pope of Alexandria. That is why the Coptic Orthodox Church is called the Church of Alexandria, and why we are his spiritual children. Long ago he came to the great city of Alexandria, preached about Jesus, and many people believed and were baptized. He loved the people there, and he served them until the end of his life. Every time we go to church, we are part of the family that St. Mark began. We can thank God for him and ask for his prayers.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Joseph the Carpenter?
text: St. Joseph was the righteous man who took care of St. Mary and baby Jesus. He worked hard as a carpenter. When an angel spoke to him in a dream, he listened to God and obeyed right away. He brought St. Mary and Jesus safely to Egypt, and later back home to Nazareth. He was gentle, quiet and trustworthy. The Church loves him as the guardian of the Holy Family. Joseph shows us that we can serve God by working honestly and by taking care of the people God gives us.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. John the Baptist?
text: St. John the Baptist was the cousin of Jesus. His parents were Zechariah and Elizabeth, and an angel told them about his birth. He lived simply and told people to turn back to God. His job was to get hearts ready for Jesus, so he is called the Forerunner. He baptized people in the Jordan River, and he baptized Jesus too. When he saw Jesus, he said Jesus is the Lamb of God. John was humble. He knew he was not the most important one, and he was happy to point to Jesus.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

verse.text: Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.

title: Who is St. Stephen?
text: St. Stephen was one of the first seven deacons of the Church. He was full of faith and the Holy Spirit, and he helped take care of widows and people in need. He spoke boldly about Jesus. Some people did not like this, and in the end he gave his life for Jesus. He is called the first martyr. Even then he was gentle: he prayed that God would forgive the people who were unkind to him. The Church calls him the Archdeacon, and the deacons in our church ask for his prayers. Stephen shows us how to forgive.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Peter the Apostle?
text: Peter was a fisherman called Simon. Jesus called him to follow Him and said, I will make you a fisher of men. Peter was one of the twelve apostles, and he was often the first to speak up. He loved Jesus very much, but once he was afraid and said he did not know Jesus. Jesus forgave him and loved him again. After Pentecost, Peter preached boldly and many people believed. His story tells us that when we make mistakes, we can say sorry, and Jesus forgives us. The Church remembers him together with St. Paul at the Feast of the Apostles.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Paul the Apostle?
text: Paul was first called Saul. At first he was against the followers of Jesus. Then Jesus appeared to him on the road to Damascus, and his life changed completely. He was baptized and became a great apostle. Paul traveled to many countries to tell people about Jesus, and he started many churches. He also wrote letters to them, called epistles, and many are in the New Testament. Paul went through many hard times, but he kept trusting God. He teaches us that anyone can change and serve Jesus with all their heart.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. George?
text: St. George was a brave soldier who loved Jesus more than anything. When the emperor told him to stop believing in Jesus, he said no and stayed faithful. He was kind and he was not afraid. The Church calls him the Prince of Martyrs. Many pictures show him on a horse, and the stories about the dragon remind us that Jesus gives us strength over evil. Many churches in Egypt and around the world are named for him. When we feel afraid to do what is right, we can remember St. George and ask for his prayers.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Mina the Wonder Worker?
text: St. Mina was a soldier in Egypt who loved to pray. He left the army and went to live in the desert as a monk, and then he told people about Jesus without fear. He is called the Wonder Worker because many people were healed and helped through his prayers. A famous monastery of St. Mina is near Alexandria, in the desert at Maryut, and people visit it from all over the world. Many Coptic children are named Mina. When we are sick or worried, we can ask St. Mina to pray for us.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Antony the Great?
text: St. Antony is called the Father of Monks. As a young man he heard the Gospel in church and wanted to follow Jesus with his whole heart. He gave what he had to the poor and went to the desert to pray. He lived simply and spent his time with God. Many people came to ask him for advice, and many became monks because of him. He showed us that prayer is powerful and that God is with us even in lonely places. His monastery near the Red Sea is still alive today.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Pachomius?
text: St. Pachomius was a monk in Upper Egypt. As a young man he was made to serve as a soldier, and he was touched by the kindness of Christians who helped strangers. He later became a Christian and then a monk. Many early monks lived alone, but Pachomius started monasteries where monks lived together. They shared the work, prayed together and ate together. This is called community life, and so he is called the Father of Community Life. His rules helped many monasteries around the world. He teaches us that we are stronger when we love, share and help each other.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Macarius the Great?
text: St. Macarius the Great was a monk who lived in the desert of Scetis in Wadi El Natrun in Egypt. He loved to pray and was known for his kindness and his patience. Many people came to learn from him, and they say he had a gentle heart. A famous monastery is named after him in the same desert, and monks still pray there today. He teaches us to be patient, to pray often and to speak kindly to everyone.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Moses the Black?
text: St. Moses the Black lived in Egypt long ago. Before he became a monk he did many wrong things. Then he heard about God's love, he said sorry from his heart and went to live in the desert of Scetis. He worked hard to become gentle and humble, and many people learned from him. He is a wonderful example of repentance, which means turning back to God. No one is too far away for God to forgive, and we can always begin again.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Bishoy?
text: St. Bishoy was a monk in the desert of Egypt who loved Jesus and loved to serve. He is often called the Perfect Man, because of his love. A well known story tells that he washed the feet of a visitor, and the Church teaches that it was Jesus who came to him. Whether or not we remember the details, the lesson is clear: when we are kind to others, we are kind to Jesus. His monastery in Wadi El Natrun is still busy with monks and visitors today.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Shenouda the Archimandrite?
text: St. Shenouda the Archimandrite was a leader of monks in Upper Egypt. He was the head of a large community of monks and nuns, and he is called the Archimandrite, which means leader of the monks. He taught them to work, pray, study the Bible and help the poor. He wrote many sermons in the Coptic language. The White Monastery near Sohag is linked to him. St. Shenouda shows us that serving God and loving the poor go hand in hand.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Demiana?
text: St. Demiana lived in Egypt and gave her life to Jesus. She was the daughter of a governor, and she gathered forty young women who prayed and served God together with her. They were brave and loved each other, and they stayed faithful to Jesus even in hard times. The Church remembers them with love. There is a famous monastery of St. Demiana in the Delta, and many girls in Egypt are named after her. Their story shows us that good friends help each other love God.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is Archangel Michael?
text: The Archangel Michael is one of God's great angels. Angels are God's servants who are sent to help us. Michael is known as the protector of God's people, and the Church asks for his prayers every month on the 12th of the Coptic month. In the Bible he is a leader who stands up for the good. We cannot see angels, but God sends them to take care of us. We can pray, Archangel Michael, please pray for us, and we do not need to be afraid.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is Archangel Gabriel?
text: The Archangel Gabriel is the angel who brings good news. God sent him to tell Zechariah that he would have a son named John. Then God sent him to St. Mary in Nazareth to tell her that she would be the mother of Jesus. He said, Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with you. We remember his message every year at the Feast of the Annunciation. God sends us good news too, in the Bible and in prayer.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Athanasius the Apostolic?
text: St. Athanasius was the 20th Pope of Alexandria, and he is called the Apostolic because he held to the faith of the apostles. When he was a young deacon, he went with his Pope to the Council of Nicea. There the Church taught clearly that Jesus Christ is truly God. Athanasius kept teaching this faith, even when powerful people were against him and he was sent away several times. Because of him, the Church is strong in the true faith. He teaches us to stand for what is true with love and courage.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Cyril the Great?
text: St. Cyril was the 24th Pope of Alexandria and is called the Pillar of the Faith. He defended the teaching that St. Mary is truly the Theotokos, which means the Mother of God, because the child she carried is God the Son. This was affirmed at the Council of Ephesus. Cyril wrote many books explaining the faith, and the Church still loves them. When we sing praises to St. Mary, we remember how Cyril and the Church honored her.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Mary of Egypt?
text: St. Mary of Egypt lived long ago. In her young life she was far from God. Then, during a visit to Jerusalem, she was moved to pray and she decided to change. She went into the desert beyond the Jordan River and lived there in prayer for many years. A priest named Zosimas met her near the end of her life. St. Mary of Egypt reminds us that no matter what has happened, God welcomes everyone who turns back to Him with all their heart.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Abanoub?
text: St. Abanoub was a young boy who loved Jesus very much. He lived in Egypt and grew up in a Christian home, and his parents taught him to pray. When he was just a boy, he was brave and said that he believed in Jesus, even though it was not easy. He kept loving Jesus until the end. The Church loves him as one of the youngest saints. Many churches are named after him, and many children are named Abanoub. He shows us that children can be heroes of faith too.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is Pope Kyrillos VI?
text: Pope Kyrillos VI was the 116th Pope of Alexandria. Before he became Pope, he was a monk named Abouna Mina who lived a simple life of prayer. He loved the Holy Liturgy and prayed it very often. As Pope, he cared for the Church with much love and prayer. Many people say that they were helped through his prayers. He teaches us that prayer is very strong, and that a humble heart is dear to God. The Church honors him as a saint.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who was Pope Shenouda III?
text: Pope Shenouda III was the 117th Pope of Alexandria. He loved the Bible and Sunday School, and he was a great teacher who helped many children and families learn about Jesus. Before he became Pope, he was a monk. He served the Church for many years and wrote many books. Many Copts remember him with love and respect. He reminds us to love the Bible and to keep learning about God.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who are the 21 Martyrs of Libya?
text: The 21 Martyrs of Libya were twenty one men who loved Jesus very much. They were Coptic Orthodox Christians, and they were working far from home. Because they believed in Jesus, they were asked to say that they did not, but they kept their faith and said His name. Our Church remembers them as saints, and we pray that they pray for us. They remind us that loving Jesus is the most important thing in the world, and that God holds His children close.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is Anba Abraam of Fayoum?
text: Anba Abraam was a bishop of Fayoum in Egypt, about a hundred years ago. He loved the poor so much that he is called the Friend of the Poor. He gave away what he received and lived simply himself. People from all kinds of homes came to him, and he cared for them all. He prayed a lot. His example shows us that giving to others with a happy heart is one way to love Jesus.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. John the Beloved?
text: St. John was one of the twelve apostles, and he is called the disciple whom Jesus loved. He stayed close to Jesus, even at the Cross, where Jesus asked him to care for St. Mary. John wrote the Gospel of John and three letters, and the book of Revelation. He taught that God is love, and that we should love one another. John teaches us to stay near to Jesus and to love others as He does.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is Archangel Raphael?
text: The Archangel Raphael is an angel who helps and heals. His name means God heals. In the book of Tobit, he walked with a young man named Tobias on a long journey, kept him safe and helped him and his family. The Church remembers Raphael as a helper in times of sickness and a guide in danger. We can ask him to pray for us and for people who are ill. God cares about us and sends His angels to watch over us.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: Who is St. Philopater Mercurius?
text: St. Philopater Mercurius was a brave Roman soldier who followed Jesus. He is also called Abu Seifein, which means the one with two swords, because pictures show him with two swords. He loved Jesus and would not give up his faith. Many churches in Old Cairo and around Egypt are named after him. He teaches us to be loyal to Jesus, no matter what.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary, Synaxarium style

title: What is the Feast of Nayrouz?
text: Nayrouz is the Coptic New Year. It begins on the first day of the month of Tout, which is usually September 11 or 12 in our calendar. The Coptic calendar began in the time of Emperor Diocletian, when many Christians were martyred. So we also call it the Era of the Martyrs, and we remember them with thankfulness. It is a time to start fresh, to thank God for another year and to ask for blessings and peace. In the Church we pray special hymns, and many families celebrate with joy.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Feast of the Cross?
text: The Feast of the Cross reminds us of the cross of Jesus. On the cross, Jesus gave His life out of love for us, and then He rose again. For us the cross is a sign of love and victory. We make the sign of the cross when we pray. In our calendar we celebrate the Feast of the Cross in the month of Tout, and there is another feast for the finding of the cross by St. Helena in the month of Baramhat. We love the cross because it shows how much Jesus loves us.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

title: What is the Annunciation?
text: The Annunciation is the day we remember when the angel Gabriel visited St. Mary. He told her that God had chosen her to be the mother of Jesus. St. Mary was humble and she said yes. She said, Let it be to me according to your word. We celebrate this feast every year, and it is a happy day. It teaches us to say yes to God, too.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is Christmas, the Nativity of Jesus?
text: The Nativity is the birthday of Jesus. We celebrate it with the Church on January 7, which is the 29th of Koiahk in the Coptic calendar. Jesus was born in Bethlehem, in a simple place, to St. Mary and with St. Joseph beside her. Angels told shepherds the good news, and wise men later came to see Him. God became a little baby because He loves us. We celebrate with the Holy Liturgy, with hymns and with joy.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is Epiphany, the Feast of Theophany?
text: Theophany means God shows Himself. It is the feast when Jesus was baptized by John in the Jordan River. The Holy Spirit came down like a dove, and the voice of the Father said, This is My beloved Son. So all three Persons of the Holy Trinity were shown. In the Coptic Church the feast is celebrated on the 11th of Tobi, which is usually January 19. It also reminds us of our own baptism.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Presentation of Jesus in the Temple?
text: When Jesus was a baby, St. Mary and St. Joseph brought Him to the temple in Jerusalem, as the law taught. There an old man named Simeon took Him in his arms and thanked God. Simeon had been waiting to see the promised Savior, and he said that Jesus is a light to all nations. A prophetess named Anna also praised God. We celebrate this feast on the 8th of Amshir. It teaches us to give our best to God.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why do we celebrate the Entry of Jesus into Egypt?
text: When Jesus was a small child, an angel warned St. Joseph in a dream to take Jesus and St. Mary to Egypt. So the Holy Family traveled to Egypt and stayed for a time, until it was safe to go back to Nazareth. Coptic tradition remembers many places in Egypt that they visited, and many churches stand there today. We celebrate this feast on the 24th of Bashans, and Egypt is called blessed because Jesus walked on its land. The prophet Isaiah said, Blessed be Egypt My people.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is Palm Sunday?
text: Palm Sunday is the day Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a donkey. The people were so happy to see Him! They waved palm branches and shouted, Hosanna, which means save us. They welcomed Him as their King. In church we hold palms and sing happy hymns, and the priest prays for us. Palm Sunday is the start of Holy Week.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is Holy Week and Pascha?
text: Holy Week is the week before Easter, and we call it Pascha. We pray special prayers each day in church and remember the last days of Jesus on earth. On Covenant Thursday we remember the Last Supper, when Jesus gave us the Eucharist, and He washed the disciples' feet. On Good Friday we remember His crucifixion, and we pray quietly and with deep love. On Saturday evening we get ready for the joy of the Resurrection. It is a serious week, but it ends with great joy.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Ascension of Jesus?
text: Forty days after His Resurrection, Jesus went up to heaven in front of His disciples. A cloud received Him, and angels told them that He will come again in the same way. Jesus did not leave us alone. He promised to send the Holy Spirit, and He sits at the right hand of the Father. We celebrate Ascension on a Thursday, forty days after Easter. It teaches us that heaven is our home, and that Jesus is always with us.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is Pentecost?
text: Pentecost is the feast of the coming of the Holy Spirit. It is fifty days after the Resurrection. The disciples were praying together in Jerusalem, and the Holy Spirit came upon them like tongues of fire. They began to speak in many languages and told people about Jesus, and many were baptized that day. We call it the birthday of the Church. The Holy Spirit helps us to pray, to love and to do what is right.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Transfiguration?
text: One day Jesus took Peter, James and John up a high mountain. There His face shone like the sun, and His clothes became bright as light. Moses and Elijah appeared and spoke with Him. A voice from the cloud said, This is My beloved Son, listen to Him. The disciples saw some of His glory. The Church celebrates this feast on the 13th of Mesra. It teaches us that Jesus is God, and that we should listen to Him.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Feast of St. Mary's Departure?
text: The Church remembers when St. Mary, the Theotokos, finished her life on earth. We say that she fell asleep in peace, and the Church teaches that the Lord took her to be with Him. The Church remembers her departure on the 21st of Tobi, and the taking of her body on the 16th of Mesra. Fifteen days before this second feast, many Copts fast to honor her. We love St. Mary as our mother in faith, and we ask for her prayers.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Wedding at Cana?
text: Jesus went with St. Mary and His disciples to a wedding in a town called Cana. During the wedding, the family ran out of wine. St. Mary told the servants, Do whatever He tells you. Jesus asked them to fill big jars with water, and the water became wine. It was His first miracle. The Church celebrates this feast in the month of Tobi. Jesus cares about our needs, and St. Mary helps us ask Him.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Finding of the Cross?
text: The Cross of Jesus was hidden for a long time. St. Helena, the mother of Emperor Constantine, was a devout Christian who wanted to find it. The Church remembers that she traveled to Jerusalem, and the Cross was found there, and a church was built on that holy place. We celebrate the finding of the Cross on the 10th of Baramhat. It reminds us to treasure the Cross, and to be thankful for the love of Jesus.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Feast of the Apostles?
text: The Feast of the Apostles remembers the twelve apostles and the saints who preached the Gospel, with special love for St. Peter and St. Paul. The apostles left everything to follow Jesus, and after Pentecost they went out to the world to tell people about Him. We would not know Jesus today without them. The feast comes at the end of the Apostles Fast, on the 5th of Abib. We thank God for their courage and ask for their prayers.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Circumcision of Jesus?
text: Eight days after He was born, Jesus was circumcised, as the law of Moses taught, and He was given the name Jesus. His name means the Lord saves. The angel had told St. Mary and St. Joseph to give Him this name. It shows that Jesus came to keep the law, and not to break it. The Church remembers this on the 6th of Tobi. It teaches us to honor the name of Jesus.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Nativity Fast?
text: The Nativity Fast helps us get ready for Christmas. It begins on the 16th of Hatour and ends on the 28th of Koiahk, just before the Feast of the Nativity. During the fast we eat plant-based food and pray more. The month of Koiahk is full of lovely hymns for St. Mary. Fasting teaches us to wait with love, to share with others and to think about Jesus.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Apostles Fast?
text: The Apostles Fast begins the day after the end of the Pentecost season and finishes on the Feast of the Apostles, the 5th of Abib. The length changes every year, because it depends on the date of Easter. The apostles fasted and prayed before they went to preach, and we follow their example. During the fast we eat plant based foods and pray more. It reminds us to be thankful for the apostles.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Fast of St. Mary?
text: The Fast of St. Mary lasts fifteen days, from the first until the fifteenth of the month of Mesra, which is in August. It leads to the Feast of St. Mary's taking up to heaven, on the 16th of Mesra. We eat plant based food and pray more, and many people sing hymns of praise to her. We fast with love for St. Mary, and she prays for us. It is a joyful and peaceful fast.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Fast of Nineveh?
text: The Fast of Nineveh is a three day fast about two weeks before Great Lent. We remember the prophet Jonah, whom God sent to the people of Nineveh. They listened, they fasted and prayed, and they turned away from doing wrong. God saw this and forgave them. The fast reminds us that God is merciful, and that He loves it when people say sorry. It also gets us ready for Great Lent.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching
